## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	# Growth — dedup local packs against the canon (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
4	consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
5	the canon now covers. It lands the run's prunes through a single PR against the repo's default branch,
6	**delivered to land** per the repo's own delivery settings. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine. The run's
7	**Context** is **binding scope — not a hint**: do not re-decide or widen it.
8	
9	> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
10	> promote task's job (canon-side).
11	
12	## Conventions used in this doc
13	
14	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
15	- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
16	  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
17	  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
18	  a cross-repo clone.
19	- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
20	  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
21	  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
22	- **The dispatch's Context narrows the *yardstick*, never the local surface.** When the Context names
23	  newly-changed canon packs ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: …"), **those packs
24	  are this run's entire yardstick**: every prune must cite a line or rule id from one of *them*, and you never
25	  widen the comparison to the rest of the mounted canon. What is *not* narrowed is the local side — **every**
26	  local item is in play against those packs, whatever it is about. (Local pack names are unrelated to canon
27	  pack names, so there is nothing to match up.) A dispatch with **no** Context block carries no such bound: the
28	  precondition emits the list only when the mounted canon moved, and its other arm — the repo's own local packs
29	  changed — deliberately emits none, so that run compares the fresh local items against the whole mounted canon.
30	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
31	  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
32	  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
33	  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.
34	
35	## Start by reading the canon window diff
36	
37	**Code-work already ran** — [worker.mjs](worker.mjs), the deterministic first phase of this task — and wrote
38	what the mounted canon **added** in this window into the tracking issue's body: per declared pack, the added
39	prose lines file by file, and the ids of any checks the window introduced. Your dispatch names that issue.
40	**Read it before opening a single local pack.**
41	
42	That brief is the run's *starting point*, not a second bound: the Context's pack list is still what a prune
43	may cite, so a local item covered by an older line in one of those packs is a legitimate prune when you can
44	quote that line. What the brief buys you is attention spent where the *new* coverage is, instead of re-reading
45	a corpus whose lines mostly predate this run. It is complete except where it says otherwise — a file whose
46	diff was too large to fetch, and a per-file line cap, are both stated in place with the remainder counted; go
47	read those files directly.
48	
49	A window in which no declared canon pack moved says so, and that run compares the repo's fresh local items
50	against the mounted canon as a whole — the same as a dispatch with no Context block.
51	
52	The [skill](../../skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md) owns what to do with the additions: which are candidates,
53	which prune nothing, and why a removed canon line is the reverse signal.
54	
55	## The method lives in the skill
56	
57	What to prune, strip, or rephrase; the keep-test (an item that says *more* than the canon stays; one that
58	only says it in repo-specific names goes); how a canon **check** covers an item more strongly than prose;
59	and the shrink-only discipline — all of that is owned by the
60	[**growth-dedup** skill](../../skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This
61	worker only frames the unattended run around it.
62	
63	## Discipline
64	
65	- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
66	  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.
67	- **Open a single PR against `main`** from a per-run-unique branch (see
68	  [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md)) — one PR for the
69	  whole run's prunes, not one per item — never a direct push. **Title the commit and the PR
70	  `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`** — the `growth-write-scope` check keys on that title to certify the
71	  run pruned only the repo's local packs. Then **deliver it by the shared procedure —
72	  [deliver-pr.md](../../../../packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md)**. That procedure — never this file — owns every
73	  landing nuance: it reads this repo's `maintenance.delivery` (a `review` repo's PR waits for the owner — still
74	  a delivered outcome) and arms auto-merge where the repo allows it. Do not assume this run's PR merges
75	  unreviewed — that is the repo's setting, not this task's (the declared ceiling is `merged-pr`: it *may*
76	  land). What holds the prune bar on the default settings is the quote-the-canon-line discipline above, the
77	  `dedup-prune-integrity` and `growth-write-scope` checks, and CI — never a reviewer's second look, which a
78	  wrongful prune is easy to wave through anyway. **Put the issue reference in the commit message** —
79	  `Refs #<n>` for this task's tracking issue (below), in the commit itself, not only the PR body. The repo's
80	  `basics` `task-lifecycle` check gates a PR on its commits referencing an issue, so a prune commit that cites
81	  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.
82	- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green before pushing.
83	
84	## The brief, and the record
85	
86	Code-work has already posted **this window's canon diff** as a comment on your own work item — the issue you
87	are reading. That comment is the brief this run starts from. **It is a required input**: a work item carrying

89	than re-deriving the window yourself.

92	as the prune: date, `growth-dedup`, what was removed and the canon line that now covers it. That file is the
93	record — there is no standing issue, and a run that pruned nothing writes no row.
94	
95	## Nothing downstream catches a wrong prune
96	
97	Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
98	this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. On the default
99	delivery settings the PR carrying a prune lands once CI passes, so there is no reviewer downstream to catch
100	what the run got wrong: a real lesson pruned on a claim the canon does not actually make is gone.
101	
102	## What this task must never do
103	
104	- **Never edit the read-only canon** — it only prunes the repo's *local packs* against it, and the
105	  `growth-write-scope` check reds a run that touches anything outside them.
106	- **Never land a prune outside a PR** — every prune rides the run's single PR, delivered by
107	  [deliver-pr.md](../../../../packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md); a direct push to `main` is never in scope, and
108	  neither is merging past a red check or a repo whose delivery setting says `review`.
109	- **Never prune a local item without quoting the mounted-canon line (or covering check rule id) that covers
110	  it** — when unsure, leave it.
111	- **Never widen the dispatch's Context.** If it named the changed canon packs, a prune citing coverage from
112	  any *other* canon pack is out of scope for this run — leave the item; the cycle that moves that pack will
113	  reach it.
114	- **Never prune a local item that makes a stronger point about a narrower case** than the canon — that isn't
115	  redundancy. (A local item that only restates the canon in repo-specific names *is* prunable once the canon
116	  covers the point.)

The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
the canon now covers. It lands the run's prunes through a single PR against the repo's default branch,
**delivered to land** per the repo's own delivery settings. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine. The run's
**Context** is **binding scope — not a hint**: do not re-decide or widen it.

> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
> promote task's job (canon-side).

## Conventions used in this doc

- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
  a cross-repo clone.
- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
- **The dispatch's Context narrows the *yardstick*, never the local surface.** When the Context names
  newly-changed canon packs ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: …"), **those packs
  are this run's entire yardstick**: every prune must cite a line or rule id from one of *them*, and you never
  widen the comparison to the rest of the mounted canon. What is *not* narrowed is the local side — **every**
  local item is in play against those packs, whatever it is about. (Local pack names are unrelated to canon
  pack names, so there is nothing to match up.) A dispatch with **no** Context block carries no such bound: the
  precondition emits the list only when the mounted canon moved, and its other arm — the repo's own local packs
  changed — deliberately emits none, so that run compares the fresh local items against the whole mounted canon.
- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.

**Code-work already ran** — [worker.mjs](worker.mjs), the deterministic first phase of this task — and wrote
what the mounted canon **added** in this window into the tracking issue's body: per declared pack, the added
prose lines file by file, and the ids of any checks the window introduced. Your dispatch names that issue.

may cite, so a local item covered by an older line in one of those packs is a legitimate prune when you can
quote that line. What the brief buys you is attention spent where the *new* coverage is, instead of re-reading
a corpus whose lines mostly predate this run. It is complete except where it says otherwise — a file whose
diff was too large to fetch, and a per-file line cap, are both stated in place with the remainder counted; go
read those files directly.

only says it in repo-specific names goes); how a canon **check** covers an item more strongly than prose;

  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.

# Vessel-image quantification — the judgment core

This project measures fluorescently-labelled cerebral vessels in the **gP-CD31 (red) confocal
panels**: categorize / count / measure. What follows is only the judgment a check cannot carry.
The enforced rules live in this pack's checks; the full working detail (overlay style knobs,
file map, calibration numbers) stays in [`analysis/WORKING-GUIDE.md`](../../../../analysis/WORKING-GUIDE.md),
and current state in [`analysis/STATUS.md`](../../../../analysis/STATUS.md).

## Never validate the pipeline against itself

Expectations come from **looking at the images** — they live in
[`expected-results.md`](../../../../references/wang-2022-cd31-vascular-network/figures/panels/expected-results.md) and are what the
automated pipeline is judged *against*. Running the pipeline and presenting its own output as the
expected result is circular and does not count as evidence.

## Progress is a visual assertion, not a table

An extraction change is discussed by **overlaying the result on the image**, checked against what it
actually misses here — faint vessels, fragmentation, thick-vessel handling. The procedure is in
[vessel-overlay-review](skills/vessel-overlay-review/SKILL.md).

## The metric definitions are locked

COUNT = branch **segments** (junction-to-junction / junction-to-tip — *not* connected components,
which are reported alongside), CATEGORIZE = **caliber**, MEASURE = **total centerline length**.
That the script keeps reporting all three is enforced (`locked-metric-fields`).

## Raw length is not comparable across figures

Each figure is at a different zoom and carries its own printed scale bar, so px→µm differs per
figure — and across papers it differs by more than 5×. Any cross-region or cross-figure comparison
uses **length density (mm/mm²) or area %** — never raw µm, and **never a mean that spans two
papers**: species, injury model, marker and magnification all change between them, which is why the
rollup is grouped per paper. This is why every working panel must stay calibrated
(`panel-scale-calibration`).

A bar is **measured off the panel**. A figure that draws no bar goes in `UNCALIBRATED` **with the
reason**, reporting area % and pixels only. The single copy is `SCALEBAR_PX` in
`analysis/measure_vessels.py` (`calibration-single-source` for code, `scale-numbers-match-calibration`
for the numbers quoted in the docs).

## A paper is finished when the PDF is redundant

The procedure is in [paper-intake](skills/paper-intake/SKILL.md).

## Say which numbers are trustworthy

Area %, length density and the µm calibration are usable; per-segment **count** is still inflated by
fragmentation, absolute length comes from figure-resolution crops, and the capillary/artery split
is one diameter threshold (`ARTERY_DIAM_PX`). When a number is not yet trustworthy, say so where it
is quoted.

Refs #256

Weekly `growth-dedup` pass — re-checks the repo's local pack
(`vascular-coloring`) against the canon packs that moved this window
(basics, claudinite-growth, claudinite-lifecycle, tidy-repo, barriers,
claude-code-web-users-support, research-project).

## What was pruned

Two `RULES.md` sections stripped to their project residue — the portable
half is now stated generically in `research-project`'s canon rules:

- **"Raw length is not comparable across figures" → "Cross-paper
  comparisons are never averaged."** The normalize/never-average-raw,
  group-by-source, single-sourced-calibration, and
  mark-uncalibrated-with-reason instructions all map onto
  `research-project` RULES.md § *"A raw measurement is comparable only
  inside one calibration"* ("Aggregate and compare only normalized
  quantities… never a mean spanning two sources that differ in more than
  scale… mark it uncalibrated with the reason"). Kept only the
  paper-specific magnitude fact (>5× scale variance) and the grouping key
  (per paper).
- **"Say which numbers are trustworthy."** Dropped the closing
  instruction ("say so where it is quoted") — covered by
  `research-project` RULES.md § *"Show, don't just tell"* ("State that
  boundary inline, beside the number, not in a separate caveats
  section"). Kept the list of which quantities in this pipeline are/aren't
  trustworthy — that judgment is domain-specific and no check carries it.

Recorded in `.claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/VERSIONS.md`
(new file — this is the pack's first dedup pass).

Everything else in the local pack (checks, skills, the rest of `RULES.md`)
is genuinely domain-specific — vessel-image calibration constants, the
locked metric definitions, overlay color rules — and isn't covered by any
of this window's canon changes, which are almost entirely internal
Claudinite task-queue/scheduler mechanics.

## Verification

- `node .claudinite/local/packs/vascular-coloring/pack.test.mjs` — 23/23 passed.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking (1 pre-existing advisory, unrelated to this change).
